evaluation.name: Project Description, Project Structure and Security Policy

children.name: Project Description
children.reason:
Evaluation of the README file:

project_purpose:
Score (avg): 5.0
[CODING] The README explains the purpose exceptionally well and from several complementary angles. The "Vision der Mobilitätsplattform" section states the goal clearly: citizens of Bamberg should plan routes via an app choosing their focus (sustainability, speed, comfort) and use/buy all modes of transport flexibly with a single ticket. The "Projektaufbau" section explains the two-part architecture (seamless linking of public transport with private and rented vehicles in both routing and payment) and honestly explains which parts are done (routing "weitgehend erreicht") and which are not (payment, due to coordination with the Verkehrsverbund Großraum Nürnberg). The "Nutzen für die Kommune" section adds the municipal benefit: data sovereignty and centralized management of street maps, timetable data, traffic-counting sensor data, exclusion zones for scooters, and ÖPNV usage data. It also links to the official smartcity.bamberg.de project page for background. This is a thorough, concrete description of both what the project does and why it is useful.

setup_instructions:
Score (avg): 2.0
[CODING] There are no actual setup instructions. The README contains no prerequisites, no installation, build or run commands, no environment/configuration guidance, and no deployment or usage steps. The only related content is a short "Technische Dokumentation" section linking to two sub-documents ("[Web App](web-app/README.md)" and "[Mobile App](mobile-app/README.md)"), which suggests that setup details may exist deeper in the repository, but the top-level README itself defers entirely to those links and gives the reader no way to get the software running. Since a reviewer/citizen receiving this repository cannot set up the project from the root README alone, the score is poor, though the pointers to sub-READMEs and the linked code/license prevent the lowest score.

info_project_status:
Score (avg): 4.0
[CODING] The project status is conveyed reasonably well, mostly through the "Meilensteine und Organisation" and "Projektaufbau" sections. The README states that publishing the open source code in September 2025 was "ein wichtiger Meilenstein" and that the project had already started parallel to the strategy development (2021–spring 2023). It also describes unfinished work: the payment function "konnte bislang nicht implementiert werden," coordination with the payment processes of the Verkehrsverbund Großraum Nürnberg was "bis 2025 nicht abgeschlossen," not all components could be open-sourced due to budget, and real-world operation in Bamberg still requires "weitere technische und nicht-technische Fragen." This clearly indicates an ongoing development project with pending items rather than an abandoned or stable one. It stops short of the highest score because there is no explicit, plainly labeled status statement (e.g., "in active development," version, release history, roadmap, or lack of maintenance) and no dates/commit activity referenced.

info_maintainer:
Score (avg): 4.0
[CODING] The README identifies the organizational actors and contributors in the "Meilensteine und Organisation" section: the initiative came from the transport division of Stadtwerke Bamberg (STVP), which became a partner of the Smart City Bamberg program and received part of the Smart City budget through a Mittelweiterleitungsvertrag to run the project independently; the code was developed "in Kooperation mit dem Bamberger Startup wikimove" (with a link to wikimove.me); and the program sponsor Smart City Bamberg is linked, along with the funding bodies BMWSB and KfW. This answers "who is behind/contributes to the project" quite well. It does not, however, name concrete maintainers or contact persons (no maintainer list, e-mail, issue tracker, contribution guidelines, or governance model), which is why it is scored 4 rather than 5.

children.name: Project Structure
children.reason:
Project structure evaluation:

directory_organization:
Score (avg): 4.0
[CODING] The repository is organized as a polyglot monorepo split by deliverable: `backend/` (Keycloak, Spring/Gradle service, routing config), `mobile-app/` (Flutter), `web-app/` (React/TypeScript), plus `logo/` and a `publiccode.yml` at the root. Each sub-project follows its stack's canonical layout: `mobile-app/` uses the standard Flutter tree (`lib/`, `lib/src/`, `test/`, `android/`, `ios/`, `assets/`, `l10n.yaml`, `pubspec.yaml`); `web-app/` uses `src/`, `public/`, `cypress/`, `scripts/`, `deploy/`, `.storybook/` with build config (`vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`) at the project root; `backend/mobility-manager-backend-svc/` uses the standard Gradle/Spring layout (`src/main/java`, `src/main/resources/{db,graphql,META-INF}`, `buildSrc/`, wrapper scripts). Weaknesses: there is no top-level `docs/` directory and no shared documentation location; binary marketing assets (`logo/KFW.png`, `Kombilogo_BMWSB_KFW.png`, `Logo_BMI.jpg`) sit at the repository root rather than under an assets/resources folder; and `backend/routing/` is a flat pile of deployment config (`elasticsearch.yml`, `pelias.json`, `docker-compose.yaml`) with no `src`-style structure. Also `backend/keycloak/` is only a vendored subset (compose file plus licence docs), which is acceptable but inconsistently scoped compared with the other backend folders. Overall organization is good and idiomatic, with only minor deviations.

naming_conventions:
Score (avg): 3.0
[CODING] Naming is broadly idiomatic per stack but inconsistent across the monorepo. Positives: Dart files use snake_case as required (`common/date_time_extension.dart`, `data/model/geo_json/`, `ui/common/compact_bottom_sheet.dart`); React components are consistently PascalCase folders with an `index.ts(x)` barrel (`components/AccountInformationModal/`, `wmv-components/WmvModal/`); hooks use the `use*` camelCase prefix (`hooks/useUrlParamsState.ts`); domain models use kebab-case directories (`models/budget-plan-membership/`, `models/vehicle-fee-pricing/`). Problems: README casing is inconsistent across modules — `README.md`, `Readme.md` (`backend/keycloak/Readme.md`, `backend/routing/nginx-proxy/Readme.md`, `otp-build/Readme.md`, `otp-config/Readme.md`) and `README.adoc` (`backend/mobility-manager-backend-svc/README.adoc`) all coexist; style file extensions are mixed between `.ts` and `.tsx` (`wmv-components/LoadingAnimation/LoadingAnimation.styles.ts` vs `components/AccountInformationModal/styles.ts` vs `ConfirmationModal.styles.tsx`); directories mix camelCase (`web-app/src/state/toUpdate/`) with kebab-case (`wmv-components`, `design-system`); and there are several outright spelling errors in file names (`assets/icons/fill/baterryLow.svg`, `biekAndScooter.svg`, `pages/Zones/ZonePlanningMode/PalnningModePreviewPredicatesView.styles.ts`, `components/TripDetailsAndManagement/TripBudgedRefundForm.tsx`). These inconsistencies make the naming convention only acceptable rather than good.

separation_of_concerns:
Score (avg): 4.0
[CODING] Concerns are generally well separated. Source, test, and configuration artefacts live in distinct locations per sub-project: `web-app` keeps application code in `src/`, E2E tests in `cypress/` (`cypress/integration/Login/Login.js`, `cypress/support/`), Storybook config in `.storybook/`, deployment config in `deploy/` (`default.conf`, `envs/.env.dev|.env.prod|.env.test`), environment files at the root (`.env.development`, `.env.production`, `.env.test`), tooling config at the root (`.eslintrc`, `.prettierrc.json`, `.stylelintrc.json`, `sonar-project.properties`, `Dockerfile`), and build helpers in `scripts/set-app-version-in-env.js`. The mobile app separates `lib/` source from `test/`, platform shells (`android/`, `ios/`), and static `assets/`, with localization isolated in `lib/l10n/*.arb` plus `l10n.yaml`. On the backend, `src/main/java` (code) is cleanly separated from `src/main/resources` (configuration, `graphql/` schemas, `db/` migrations). Deductions: there is no `src/test` tree at all for `backend/mobility-manager-backend-svc`, so the backend has no visible unit-test separation; unit tests in `web-app` are scattered inside `src` rather than centralized (`components/Header/Header.test.tsx`, `components/CustomPopover/CustomPopover.test.tsx`, `services/UserService.test.ts`, `state/toUpdate/*.test.ts`, `hooks/__tests__/useUrlParamsState.test.tsx`, `zone/tests/ZoneVisibilityNextEvaluationPoint.test.ts`), and a test fixture (`zone_next_evaluation_point_test.xlsx`) is committed alongside production services code. `mobile-app/test/` holds only a single `widget_test.dart`, which is thin.

modularity:
Score (avg): 4.0
[CODING] The codebase is decomposed into coherent modules along functional boundaries. `web-app/src` has a clear layering: `components/` (feature UI such as `CustomerDatabase/`, `TripDetailsAndManagement/`, `VehicleInformationModal/`), a reusable design system (`wmv-components/` with per-component folders plus barrels, `design-system/NewDataTable.tsx`), domain models split by bounded context (`models/budget-plan/`, `models/budget-plan-membership/`, `models/trip/`, `models/fleet-management/`, `models/common/`), services grouped by domain (`services/zone/`, `services/trip/`, `services/layer-management/`), state slices (`state/app/`, `state/common/`, `state/zones-management/`), plus cross-cutting folders (`hooks/`, `atoms/`, `plugins/`, `utils/`, `configs/`). The mobile app mirrors this with `lib/src/data/` (repositories and models per domain), `lib/src/ui/` (feature packages `home/`, `itinerary/`, `routing/` with cubit/state/page/content per feature), `lib/src/common/`, and DI isolated in `lib/src/di.dart`. The backend splits `buildSrc` build logic from application code and keeps `resources/db` and `resources/graphql` as distinct concerns, and the routing stack is split into `nginx-proxy/`, `otp-build/`, `otp-config/` with their own Readmes. Minor modularity problems: `web-app/src/assets/map/generated_markers/` duplicates the entire marker set across `2x/`, `3x/`, and a flat copy at the same level (hundreds of identical filenames), and icon libraries (`assets/icons/fill`, `outline`) are flat directories with 150+ files each, which reduces navigability; `state/toUpdate/` is an opaque module name. These are organizational blemishes rather than structural flaws.
